source: closed-form from _spec/03 R-REALS-2 plus Buildings CDL.Reals.PID.mo/PIDWithReset.mo wiring; independent re-derivation
input: default controllerType=PI; k=0.37, Ti=0.3, Ni=default 0.9, xi_start=0.11, y_reset=0.275, yMin=-0.35, yMax=0.45; trigger rises at t=0.3 and t=0.7; dt=0.1 decimal grid
reference_rule: Same limited PI recurrence as PID, with the canonical PIDWithReset.mo parameter reset applied at the event: at a sample after the first where trigger is true and was false at the previous sample, xI := y_reset - yP from that sample's error before y is emitted, so the reset sample emits y=max(yMin,min(yP+xI,yMax)), and that sample's xI update is skipped (its Euler step covers the interval before the event). No reset fires at the first sample (initialisation). Rows t=0.3 and t=0.7 emit the reset target; rows t=0.4 and t=0.8 hold the same P term with the trigger high, so they emit it again before integrating.
fp_residue_note: The stimulus avoids the G36 dyadic PID cone: k=0.37, Ti=0.3, Ni=0.9, and dt=0.1 are all non-dyadic decimal literals in binary64, so k/Ti and the accumulated xI values carry rounding residue. PIDWithReset row 5 drives lower saturation after a non-dyadic reset state, so anti-windup contributes a non-dyadic correction before later reset-target rows.
format: Modelica CombiTimeTable CSV (_spec/07 §9); signal CSV is time+one output; reference.csv is time+inputs+all outputs; ryu shortest-round-trip f64
